ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and rolling 30-day screening of all directors, officers, and UBOs against: (i) OFAC SDN List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Canadian autonomous sanctions lists administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky), and the United Nations Act; (iv) FINTRAC reportable indications and media; (v) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) standards under FINTRAC Guidance 6G, requiring enhanced due diligence for PEPs, close associates, and family members; (vi) Interpol and CSIS open-source checks. Adverse findings require filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with FINTRAC within 30 days, refusal of the relationship, and immediate re-screening. Residential and corporate documentation must be verified under a risk-based approach consistent with PCMLTFA Part 1 and FINTRAC record-keeping and verification requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Quebec provincial incorporation: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (NUANS name search and decision of conformity issued through REQ single-window portal). Federal CBCA incorporation alternative: Corporations Canada — https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/cd-dgc.nsf/eng/home
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), a Quebec business corporation name must be in French: either a French-language name, or the French version of a recognized foreign trademark or a name registered under the Trademarks Act (RSC 1985, c T-13). The legal element must be in French: 'inc.', 'corp.', 'ltée', 'corporation' or 'société par actions'; English suffixes such as 'Ltd.' or 'Co.' are not accepted for Quebec provincial incorporation unless a French equivalent is adopted. For federal corporations, the name may be English, French, or bilingual and must not create confusion with existing names under CBCA Regulation s. 17. Transliteration of non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese characters) into French or English is required, and the name must be pronounceable in the language used; a legal transliteration certificate may be required by the REQ for names originating in non-Latin alphabets.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Assurance', 'Insurance', 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Fiducie' – prior authorization from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) / Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) required
'Royal', 'Reine', 'Queen', 'Régie' – prior approval from the Ministère de la Justice or the Lieutenant-Governor in Council required
'Canada' – federal authorization required before use in a corporate name
'Police', 'Gendarmerie', 'RCMP', 'Gouvernement', 'Government' – strictly prohibited as misleading public-body connotations
Terms contravening public order, public morality, or suggesting unlawful connection to a public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In Quebec, if the REQ refuses a name (refusal of decision of conformity): (i) within 30 days of the refusal, file a written reconsideration request with the REQ through the online portal, attaching the NUANS search certificate and a legal memorandum demonstrating distinctiveness and non-confusion; (ii) if reconsideration is denied, file an administrative review application with the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) under the Act respecting administrative justice (CQLR c J-3) within 30 days of the refusal; (iii) judicial review may be sought in the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of the TAQ decision. Alternatively, the fastest remedy is to re-file under a revised alternate name with a fresh NUANS search. There is no statutory extension of the 90-day reservation window; the reservation lapses if articles are not filed in time. For federal corporations, an appeal may be filed with the Director under s. 12 of the CBCA.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable with conditions: the registered office (siège social) must be a real, physical street address located in Quebec where legal process can be personally served during normal business hours; a commercial virtual office or serviced suite is permissible if the provider is authorized to accept service and the address is not a post-office box. For this creative outsourcing industry (AAA game 3D art and rigging), no physical retail or production premises are required; staff may operate remotely. If the corporation later carries on business outside Quebec (e.g., Ontario), an extra-provincial registration may be required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5-10% annual probability). The REQ and Revenu Québec do not conduct routine unannounced physical inspections for low-risk, non-licensed service corporations; however, unannounced verification may occur upon third-party complaints, irregularities in filings, or CRA payroll/GST/HST audit activity. The 'Low_Risk_Standard' AML tier and absence of statutory licensing materially reduce inspection frequency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1, arts. 2, 14-23 (incorporeation), 28-30 (share capital), 117-119 (organization and by-laws)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, a component of the Quebec Ministry of Finance)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) filed electronically via CLIC
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA); no escrow account is required by law. Authorized share capital must be described in the articles; subscribers need not deposit funds before issuance, but the board must issue shares for valid consideration and record amounts in the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions to the issued share capital set forth in the schedule appended to this resolution are accepted, and shares are accordingly issued to each subscriber; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [Street Address], [City], Quebec, and that the corporate records and minute book shall be maintained at such address as required by law; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual shareholders' meeting or until any successor is appointed; AND FURTHER RESOLVED, that the directors and officers are authorized to execute and deliver all documents and take all measures necessary to complete the incorporation and to carry out the corporate governance of the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online CLIC name-search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the online CLIC name search portal, verify that the proposed corporate name is distinct and lawful in Quebec, and submit a name reservation declaration. Provide any required legal opinion if the name contains protected elements. The name is reserved for 120 days after approval.
required_dossiers: Filled name declaration form (Proposition de nom)
Optional professional legal opinion if name contains regulated terms
Payment receipt for name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, modify the proposed name and submit a new request online; the remedy is procedural and does not affect previously filed incorporation documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – CLIC electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation electronically in CLIC, selecting the class and number of shares, any restrictions on share transfers, and the initial directors. Include the reserved name reference number, declare the legal address, and submit for payment. Confirm that the form is signed in accordance with the QBCA.
required_dossiers: Consent of initial directors if forming the corporation without incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of refusal, identify the specified deficiency in the notice, correct the articles or attachments, and resubmit through the same portal within the required deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – issuance and registration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registraire issues the Certificate of Constitution and assigns a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Confirm the certificate details, including corporate name, registered office, and director information. Use the certificate to open bank accounts and proceed with governance steps.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered Articles of Incorporation
List of initial directors if filed separately
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or contains a clerical error, request corrected or priority processing via the online certified-results portal; if substance is defective, file rectifying articles as provided under the QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Governance Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Corporate Secretary (internal corporate governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a statutory organizational meeting of the initial directors. Adopt the first board resolution, approve by-laws, confirm the registered office, and designate officers. Execute share certificates and maintain the corporate minute book and share register in accordance with the QBCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural defect is identified, ratify the matter by unanimous shareholder resolution and correct the minutes; all corporate records must be kept available for the Registrar upon request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applies to NAICS 541430 / ISIC 7490 professional and technical services; the relevant local permit office is the municipal planning, permits, and inspection department of the city where the studio is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial occupancy permit (Certificat d'occupation) issued by the local municipality for the office/studio premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no environmental impact assessment required for low-impact professional office/art studio services without industrial discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions; sanitary wastewater is discharged to the municipal sewer. Electronic waste and other hazardous items (e.g., batteries, ink cartridges) must be handled in accordance with municipal hazardous waste collection rules. Compliance with the Quebec Clean Water Act and Clean Air Act applies only if a separate physical manufacturing operation is added later.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: certification under the Quebec Fire Safety Code and local fire prevention service inspection. Occupational health: CNESST (Quebec Workplace Health and Safety) registration and compliance. Structural: any fit-out requiring structural modification must obtain a municipal building permit and an inspection by an engineer or architect under RBQ (Régie du bâtiment du Québec) rules to ensure structural load compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (www.canada.ca/cra) and Revenu Québec (www.revenuquebec.ca); Quebec administers the federal GST/HST for businesses registered in Quebec. Provincial corporate registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act; the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) is issued automatically by the Registraire des entreprises if incorporated provincially. Step 2: Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) via CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or by filing Form RC1; for CBCA corporations the BN is created upon filing articles of incorporation. Step 3: Register for GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) through Revenu Québec using the combined registration process (TPS/TVQ), which provisions the BN accounts to CRA. Step 4: Register for the federal corporate income tax account (RC account) and Quebec corporate tax account (CO account) with Revenu Québec; if hiring employees, also register for payroll source deductions (CRA and Revenu Québec DP/JP accounts). Step 5: Keep the BN/QST registration effective from the earlier of (a) the first taxable supply in Canada or Quebec and (b) the day the $30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box exists; a Canadian business corporation is per se a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act (ITA) and Part IV of the Quebec Taxation Act and is resident by incorporation (ITA s. 250(4)(a)). Relevant elections: (i) GST/HST s. 156 election and corresponding QST election for supplies between closely related Canadian corporations (nil-consideration treatment); (ii) ITA s. 216(1) election for non-residents earning Canadian-source rents or royalties on a net basis (relevant if the studio licenses its 3D art IP to Canadian licensees); (iii) ITA s. 217 election for non-resident personal services; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.4–18.6 apply ex lege, not by election, and deny interest deductions where the corresponding amount is deductible in a hybrid foreign jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Quebec Sales Tax (QST) under the Quebec Sales Tax Act (CQLR, c. T-0.1), administered by Revenu Québec in fiscal harmonization with the federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) does not apply in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (ITA-equivalent small-supplier rule; ETA s. 240 and QSTA s. 28.0.1). A Quebec resident corporation exceeding this threshold must register for GST and QST. Non-resident suppliers must register if they carry on business in Canada and exceed the same threshold, unless their supplies are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada or Quebec. GST/HST and QST invoices must contain prescribed content (seller name, BN, date, description, tax amounts; s. 169 and s. 223 ETA; s. 34 of the QST Regulation). E-invoicing is voluntary and aligned with the Pan-Canadian Peppol ecosystem; Revenu Québec requires registered businesses to issue invoices on request and to make electronic books and records available for audit in Quebec.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of services to a non-resident client (e.g., a foreign game publisher) are zero-rated under s. 7, Part V, Schedule VI of the ETA where the services are not performed in connection with real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance. Transfers of intangible personal property (3D assets, rigs, character models, licences, source files) for use outside Canada are zero-rated under s. 10 of Part V, Schedule VI. QST applies parallel zero-rating under ss. 27.1 and 28 of the QSTA Regulation. The recipient must be a non-resident person who is not registered under the ETA/QSTA and who is not acquiring the service for consumption in Canada; digital place-of-supply rules (ETA s. 142.2) deem the supply to be made in Canada if the recipient's establishment is in Canada. The exporter must not zero-rate supplies to Canadian residents, registered non-residents, or Canadian establishments of foreign clients.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable: no customs export declaration, bill of lading, or inward remittance certificate is generated for intangible digital exports; the following documentary set is the acceptable substitute evidence.
Signed Service Agreement / Statement of Work identifying the non-resident client, the scope of 3D art services, and the transfer or licence of intangible property rights.
Zero-rated tax invoice containing the supplier's Business Number and QST registration number, an explicit 'zero-rated export supply' notation, and a precise description of the digital deliverables.
Proof of digital delivery: encrypted file-transfer logs, handover certificates, email chains, or platform extraction records showing transmission to an address outside Canada.
Proof of settlement from a foreign bank account: SWIFT/IBAN wire transfer records, foreign currency receipts, or PayPal transaction logs.
Evidence of the client's non-resident status: foreign corporate registry extract, foreign tax identification number, or a signed declaration that the client is not registered for GST/HST/QST.
If the client is a related party, transfer-pricing documentation under ITA s. 247 and a legal memorandum on place-of-supply analysis.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may audit export zero-rating claims and reassess within the normal 4-year period, extended to 7 years for misrepresentation attributable to neglect or carelessness, and without time limit for fraud. Where zero-rating is overturned, the supplier must remit the full 14.975% GST/QST on the consideration plus daily compound interest (ETA s. 280.1; QSTA s. 69). Civil penalties include the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the understated tax for false statements (ETA s. 285; analogous QSTA penalty), plus recovery of any input tax credits or rebates claimed in respect of the export. Criminal prosecution for intentional evasion (ETA s. 280) may lead to fines and imprisonment. The 180-day settlement benchmark is an internal credit-control practice rather than a statutory CRA deadline; unduly deferred withheld receivables from non-residents may attract ITA s. 15(2) shareholder-benefit or s. 80.4(2) imputation assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); foreign exchange administration oversight is coordinated with Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CFT.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency under a floating exchange rate regime. There are no general exchange controls under the Currency Act or the Bank of Canada Act; current account transactions and capital account transactions are freely permitted. Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriation are unrestricted, subject to corporate law solvency tests and ordinary tax compliance (e.g., withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, subject to treaty relief). Non-resident investors face no statutory FX approval hurdles; payments are processed through the Canadian Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) and SWIFT.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists. Canadian law does not impose a conversion ratio or statutory timeline for repatriating export receipts. Exporters may hold foreign currency accounts domestically or offshore and are required to report transactions under FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., $10,000 CAD or equivalent for large cash or cross-border transfers) and maintain books and records in accordance with the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act (GST/HST).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/EUR/USD) and optionally a Capital Escrow Account for investor funds
Operational Account with business deposit and payment solutions
Operational Account and Cross-Border USD/EUR Account
Operational Account; strong Quebec-based presence sufficient for CA_QC entity banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary settlement volume, Low for primary treasury banking. Authorized foreign fintechs or EMIs with a Canadian money-services business (MSB) registration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) may provide multi-currency accounts and cross-border payment rails, but they cannot replace a Schedule I bank due to OSFI oversight requirements, CDIC insurability, and credit facility access. Non-registered offshore EMIs are legally prohibited from providing payment services to Canadian resident businesses; any such arrangement would trigger regulatory enforcement and bank de-risking risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is not a universal legal mandate, but each Canadian Schedule I bank applies a risk-based approach. For a Quebec business corporation with Canadian directors, remote video KYC is generally acceptable for low-risk accounts. However, a foreign-owned or newly incorporated private company with no established banking relationship may be required to have at least one director, officer, or authorized signatory attend an in-branch interview at the bank's discretion, particularly when opening a Capital Escrow Account or when signatories are resident outside Canada. Certain banks require notarized corporate resolutions and proof of authority. Practical compliance: arrange physical presence for the principal director in Quebec or Toronto to avoid rejection; otherwise initiate online application via BMO or NBC with notarized KYC documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus: beneficial owners or directors residing in or transacting with sanctioned or FATF-monitored jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extracts (Quebec Registraire des entreprises and federal Corporations Canada), 90-day utility bill or lease agreement evidencing physical business presence in Quebec, notarized beneficial ownership declaration, source of wealth statements, tax clearance certificates from Revenu Québec and the CRA, and a detailed commercial explanation of cross-border client contracts and payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATF/OECD flagged B2B payment pattern: expected high-volume FX transactions with digital asset or cryptocurrency-linked counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated copies of executed master service agreements, invoices and work orders to third-party AAA game studios, proof of delivery for 3D art assets, fee explanations aligned with arm's length rates, anti-money-laundering compliance manual, counterparty KYC/extended due diligence files, and FINTRAC MSB registration certificate if using in-house payment conversion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate large capital injection or capital escrow funding from a non-resident related party or offshore holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart and group ownership structure, notarized shareholder resolution authorizing funding, financing or loan agreements, personal and corporate bank statements proving source of funds, tax opinion or legal opinion confirming compliance with Part XIII withholding and transfer-pricing rules, and a funds-flow forecast showing the stated purpose of working capital or investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate invoice timing or round-dollar wire receipts with low corporate revenue history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Game art production milestone tracker, revision/change-order documentation, project confirmations with publishers or clients, cost breakdowns per asset and rigging stage, employee/subcontractor payroll evidence, and management accounts showing the consistency of projected cash flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funds must be wired via SWIFT to a Canadian clearing institution (ACSS/Interac for domestic integration) using the legal entity name in the benefitting bank account. Recommended purpose codes include: for investment or capital contribution, use Canadian bank internal purpose descriptions and ISO 20022 instruction codes such as 'CORP' or 'GIFT' where permitted; for intercompany funding, route as 'Intercompany Loan' with purpose code 'LEND'; for trade-related advance payments, use 'TRDP'. Provide the receiving bank with a funds-flow letter, board resolution, and source-of-wealth documentation for amounts above CAD 100,000. For payments from US clients, ACH or Fedwire into a USD clear account held in Canada is permissible, with conversion to CAD via spot or forward. Verification requirements: proof of source of funds, FINTRAC reporting if transfer exceeds CAD 10,000 or if instructed by bank KYC, and no exchange-control approval needed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements to offshore 3D art studios, preferred rails are (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to suppliers/contractors; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit) only when contractually required by a major publisher or platform; (3) SWIFT MT202/MT202COV for cover instructions if using correspondent banks; and (4) domestic ACSS payment channels or Interac e-Transfer for low-value Canadian disbursements. Use service-based payment timing linked to acceptance certificates for delivered game assets. Maintain a complete audit trail of invoices and acceptance documents. For subcontractor payments in India/China/Philippines, utilize USD/EUR via local payout aggregators that are FINTRAC-exempt or registered, ensuring the Canadian bank remains the remitting institution; do not rely on personal PayPal for corporate disbursements. Recurring payroll and contractor disbursements can be batched through the bank's automated clearing house integration (Payroll Direct Deposit) and cross-border via SWIFT file activation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts (CAD/USD/EUR) with Canadian Schedule I bank treasury desks for immediate conversion of multi-currency revenue
Outright FX forwards (maturity up to 24 months) to fix conversion rates on committed client payments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging emerging-market currency exposure where the underlying currency is non-convertible or restricted, subject to bank internal eligibility and credit limits
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term intercompany loans or capital leases involving USD/EUR/CAD funding
FX swap (rollover) transactions for simultaneous spot and forward trade combinations to manage liquidity across the USD/CAD book
Vanilla FX call/put options or collars as over-the-counter derivatives with a regulated Canadian counterparty, subject to bank derivative qualification review and IFRS 9 hedge accounting requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end; calendar-year-end filers must file by the 60th day following December 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty on late filing; failure for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to cancel the enterprise's registration or dissolve the corporation; directors may incur personal liability for acts carried out after dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA) — applicable only if the corporation is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing may result in administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada under the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; calendar-year-end filers must file no later than June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; additional penalties for repeated failures and interest accruals; directors and officers may be liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17 and Quebec shareholder/beneficial-owner schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; calendar-year-end filers must file no later than June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty and compounded interest follow Revenu Québec's taxation rules; directors may be liable for unpaid amounts attributable to withheld tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (for annual GST/HST registrants whose reporting period is the fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the reporting period; for a calendar-year filer, no later than March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty (5% of the balance due plus 1% per month, maximum 12 months) and daily interest; director liability may be asserted for unremitted GST/HST.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required for distributing corporations (publicly listed or registered securities) and where a shareholder holding at least 5% of the voting shares demands an audit. A non-distributing private business corporation may waive the annual audit by unanimous shareholder resolution and may instead prepare a review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must use IFRS; private enterprises may use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook; financial statements must be prepared in Canadian dollars (CAD) unless the functional currency is otherwise determined.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In Quebec, the annual declaration must confirm and update each beneficial shareholder ('actionnaire bénéficiaire') holding 25% or more of the voting shares or exercising effective control. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded promptly in the Register of Members and, for CBCA corporations, in the Register of Individuals with Significant Control within 15 days of the transfer; the Quebec annual declaration must be filed each year even when no share transfer occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 to CAD 600 per year (approximately USD 185 to USD 445) for a registered office or corporate agent in Quebec.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 5,000 to CAD 15,000 per year (approximately USD 3,700 to USD 11,100) for a certified audit of a small private game-art outsourcing corporation, depending on transaction volume and scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); 14.0% combined rate for qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holidays. Effective rate reductions are available via the Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for others), Quebec SR&ED tax credits, Quebec interactive digital media/video game tax credits, accelerated capital cost allowance for computer hardware and software, and foreign tax credits under ITA sections 113 and 126.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via certified E-file software or CRA My Business Account. Quebec: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return filed through Revenu Québec's clicSURaffaires portal. Mandatory electronic filing applies for corporate returns prepared by tax professionals and for corporations exceeding the gross revenue threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing of T2 and CO-17. Tax instalments are payable monthly or quarterly based on prior-year taxable income and corporate tax payable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 and CO-17 must be filed no later than six months after the end of the taxation year. Balance-due taxes must be paid no later than the last day of the second month after the taxation year-end for non-CCPCs, and the last day of the third month for CCPCs claiming the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from worldwide business operations, including 3D art outsourcing contracts, asset licensing, character rigging service fees, and reimbursable production costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation without a Canadian permanent establishment should not be subject to Part I tax on ordinary foreign business income; if a Canadian PE exists, include only PE-attributable revenue and support the allocation with contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative expenses, including payroll, software subscriptions, equipment leasing, professional fees, marketing, rent, utilities, and data communication costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may deduct expenses only to the extent wholly applicable to Canadian-source PE income; intercompany and head-office charge allocations must satisfy the arm's length standard under ITA section 247 and be supported by schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses before non-operating items, including depreciation and amortization, foreign exchange losses, and administrative overhead allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be reasonable and evidenced by invoices, contracts, and bank records; reimbursements to foreign related parties must be priced at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or loss before special deductions and loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation earning Canadian business income must calculate taxable income as if the PE were an independent enterprise, using its own capital, assets, and personnel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1, Parts I to VI
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal base tax, abatement, and applicable tax credits (investment tax credits, foreign tax credits, and Quebec provincial credits claimed through the federal form).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-based reductions are not taken on the T2; withholding obligations are governed by Part XIII and cross-border service withholding under Regulation 105.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; for repeat offenders within three years, 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. CRA and Revenu Québec also charge daily compounded prescribed-rate interest on unpaid balances, late-instalment penalties, and failure-to-report-information penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents of Canada, subject to income tax treaty reduction. Under the Canada-United States treaty, the rate is generally 15%, reduced to 5% for dividends paid to a corporate beneficial owner that owns at least 10% of the voting shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a certificate of residence (TRC) from the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction and, where required by the CRA, file Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty for a Non-Resident Person) before payment. The Canadian payer must conduct reasonable due diligence, retain the TRC and NR301, and apply the treaty rate. If tax was over-withheld, the non-resident may apply to the CRA for a refund using Form NR7-R within two years after the calendar year in which the tax was withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding is 25% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly reduce copyright royalties to 10% and commercial interest to 0% to 15%. Reduced rates require a valid TRC and NR301 filed with the CRA before reliance; interest paid to unrelated arm's length financial institutions is frequently treaty-exempt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada prescribes no general CAD monetary threshold exempting non-arm's length cross-border transactions from transfer pricing documentation. ITA section 247(4) requires contemporaneous documentation to be prepared before the T2 filing date. Country-by-Country Reporting and the associated Master File become mandatory when the multinational enterprise group has consolidated annual revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000; CRA may request a Local File for controlled transactions of any size.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regime comparable to certain offshore jurisdictions, but ITA section 245 (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) and section 247 require genuine commercial substance and arm's length pricing. A 3D-art outsourcing studio must demonstrate real employees, active project management, owned or leased production infrastructure, substantive client contracts, and identifiable commercial risk; a shell arrangement will be disregarded and recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating or omitting revenue from foreign 3D art clients, fabricating purchase invoices, diverting payments into personal or nominee bank accounts, or filing an incomplete T2/CO-17.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA section 239, tax evasion is punishable on indictment by a fine of at least 50% and up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. A gross negligence penalty under ITA section 163(2) equal to 50% of the understated tax may also be assessed, plus daily compounded arrears interest. Revenu Québec imposes parallel sanctions under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct, authorize, or participate in evasion may lose limited liability protection via the corporate-veil doctrine, become jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties, and interest, and face asset seizure, court-ordered travel restrictions, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Filing and Source Deduction Remittance Failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file the T2/CO-17 within six months after year-end or failure to deduct, withhold, and remit employee income tax, Canada Pension Plan contributions, Quebec Parental Insurance Plan premiums, and employment insurance premiums.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The corporation is liable for late-filing penalties of 5% to 10% of unpaid tax plus monthly surcharges of 1% to 2%, daily prescribed-rate interest, and penalties for unremitted source deductions of up to 20% of the amount. Quebec assessments follow the same principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under ITA section 227.1 and corresponding Quebec legislation, directors are personally liable for 100% of unremitted source deductions and associated interest and penalties, even if the corporation is dissolved or bankrupt; the due-diligence defence requires proof of reasonable supervision of payroll and remittance systems.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Bare Shell Structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing through a non-arm's length offshore shell company that lacks real employees, assets, or functions; pricing intellectual-property royalties or game art services outside the arm's length range; failing to prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess to the arm's length price, impose a 10% transfer-pricing penalty under ITA section 247(3), assert gross negligence penalties under ITA section 163(2), and apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule to deny tax benefits. Interest continues to run until payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false intercompany agreements or control sham pricing may be treated as the directing minds of a fraudulent arrangement; the corporate veil is pierced, making them personally liable for civil restitution, and criminal prosecution may include imprisonment and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and International Wire Irregularities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring bank wires to avoid reporting, accepting unexplained third-party payments, commingling corporate funds with personal assets, using unregistered money service businesses for cross-border client settlements, or deliberately failing to comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the PCMLTFA can trigger administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 per violation for entities and CAD 1,000,000 for individuals; criminal money laundering under the Criminal Code carries imprisonment up to ten years, forfeiture of proceeds, and ancillary orders restricting travel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who directs routing of illicit funds, approves undocumented cash-equivalent payments, or participates in laundering faces criminal prosecution, personal asset forfeiture, travel bans, and loss of corporate limited-liability protection.
